Report_ID: Duration of common cold symptoms (days to complete resolution)
Title: Zinc nasal gel for the treatment of common cold symptoms: A double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
Author: Hirt, Nobel, & Barron
Comment: M_diff computed as group_2_mean - group_1_mean (9.0 - 2.3 = 6.7 days, positive favours zinc) from the two explicitly reported means of a simple two-group between-subjects comparison. Paper reports only "p < 0.05" (recorded as 0.05, an upper bound) with no test statistic, df, or confidence interval. The dispersion values (±0.9, ±2.5) are treated as SDs per the Methods statement that "standard deviations were calculated"; the paper does not explicitly label them as SD vs SE in the Results text. Analysed Ns assumed equal to randomized Ns (108/105) as no attrition is reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Zinc nasal gel (Zicam, zinc gluconate 33 mmol/L ionic zinc)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults with recent-onset (≤24 hr) naturally acquired common cold symptoms, recruited at four sites in the Los Angeles area

Report_ID: Duration of the common cold (time to resolution of all cold symptoms, days)
Title: Zinc Gluconate Lozenges for Treating the Common Cold in Children: A Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Macknin ML, Piedmonte M, Calendine C, Janosky J, Wald E
Comment: Paper reports MEDIAN time to resolution with 95% CIs (Kaplan-Meier/Brookmeyer-Crowley), not means with SDs; no mean duration or SD is reported anywhere, so a mean difference in days cannot be computed from the paper's own numbers. The 95% CIs are swapped between the Results text (placebo 8-9, zinc 7-10) and the Abstract/Table 3 (placebo 7-10, zinc 8-9); Table 3/Abstract values were used here. The CI bounds entered in group_*_ci_lower/upper are confidence intervals for the MEDIAN, not IQRs or ranges. The mean +/- SD values elsewhere in the paper (e.g. 10.1 +/- 3.9) are baseline SEVERITY SCORES, not duration.; unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Participant type: children and adolescents in grades 1-12 with naturally acquired common cold of <24 hours duration
Recruitment source: Two suburban school districts (Beachwood and Mayfield), Cleveland, Ohio
Outcome measurement: Median time to resolution of all cold symptoms in days (Kaplan-Meier estimate with 95% CI by Brookmeyer-Crowley method); P value from Cox proportional hazards regression
Outcome variable: Duration of the common cold (time to resolution of all cold symptoms, days)
outcome_family: duration of the common cold (days to resolution)
